stimuli.title: Charu, Bina, Kiran, Hema, Esha, Riya, Ovi, Pia occupy eight flats on floors 1 (bottom) to 4 (top). Each floor has Flat A to the west of Flat B. Each flat has one resident. For ordering only, count Floor 1 A, Floor 1 B, Floor 2 A, Floor 2 B, and so on.
stimuli.body:
Use all the following clues:
• Charu occupies floor 4, flat B.
• Kiran and Riya live in the same flat letters.
• Bina lives below Pia.
• Esha lives above Riya.
• The floor numbers of Charu and Riya differ by 1.
• Riya and Pia live in the same flat letters.
• Charu and Ovi live in the same flat letters.
• The floor numbers of Esha and Ovi differ by 1.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some bonds are cheques. All cheques are lockers. No lockers is a cards.
Conclusions:
I. Some bonds are lockers.
II. Some cheques are cards.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: No bonds is a cheques. Some cheques are lockers. All lockers are cards.
Conclusions:
I. All bonds are cards.
II. Some cards are cheques.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few bonds are cheques. All cheques are lockers. No lockers is a cards.
Conclusions:
I. Some bonds are not cheques.
II. No cheques is a cards.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few bonds are cheques. Some cheques are lockers. All lockers are cards.
Conclusions:
I. All bonds are cards.
II. No cheques is a cards.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: R < P > S < Q > U.
Conclusions: I. U ≤ Q   II. P ≥ U.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
savings rural secure = lu vo mi
savings access credit = su vo ze
rural access growth = lu re ze
secure credit growth = su mi re
savings rural growth = re vo lu
What is the code for “credit”?
questions.explanation: Answer: su. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: savings = vo, rural = lu, secure = mi, access = ze, credit = su, growth = re.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 49 km east, turns left and walks 36 km, then turns left and walks 22 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 45. Net displacement is 27 km east and 36 km north. By Pythagoras, √(27² + 36²) = 45 km.

questions.stem: H is the mother of G. A is the son of G. F is the father of G. How is A related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. F is a parent of G, and A is G’s son. Hence A is F’s grandchild.

questions.stem: G is the brother of A. A is the mother of E. B is the father of G and A. How is G related to E?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. G is the brother of E’s mother A. Therefore G is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: H is the only daughter of C. C is the father of H. B is the son of H. D is the sister of C. How is C related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. C is the father of H, and H is B’s mother. Thus C is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 60 candidates, a candidate is 16th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 42. New front rank = 16+3 = 19. Back rank = 60 − 19 + 1 = 42.

questions.stem: In a queue of 64 candidates, a candidate is 10th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 51. New front rank = 10+4 = 14. Back rank = 64 − 14 + 1 = 51.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1750. It is marked above cost and sold at a 20% discount on marked price, earning 20% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 2625. Selling price = 1750 × 120/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.8 = 2625.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 32 days and B in 48 days. They work together for 3 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need?
questions.explanation: Answer: 27. Use 96 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 96 − 3×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: A boat travels 308 km downstream and the same distance upstream. Its still-water speed is 18 km/h and stream speed is 4 km/h. Find the total time (hours).
A invests ₹36000 for 12 months. B invests ₹144000 for 5 months. Total profit is ₹105600. Find B’s share (₹).
questions.explanation: Answer: 66000. Capital-time ratio = 12 : 20. B’s share = total × 20/(32) = 66000.

questions.stem: What is the difference (₹) between compound interest and simple interest on ₹22000 at 20% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
questions.explanation: Answer: 880. For 2 years, CI − SI = P(r/100)² = 22000 × (20/100)².

questions.stem: A vessel contains 75 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 15. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 15.

questions.stem: The average of 24 numbers is 60. One number, 72, is replaced and the average rises by 7. What is the new number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 240. Total increases by 24 × 7. New number = 72 + 168.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 4 years, their combined age will be 76 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 51. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 8 = 76; x = 17, so father = 51.

questions.stem: A train of length 200 m crosses a 160 m platform at 50.4 km/h. Find crossing time in seconds (to two decimals).
A village has 4800 registered customers. This increases by 25% in year 1 and decreases by 10% in year 2. What is the final number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 5400. Apply successive factors: 4800 × 125/100 × 90/100.
